about: The hand-written parts of the lemma review sheet: its prose, and per token the Whitaker, Why and Recommend cells and `ok`, the override row that answering `ok` writes. Everything else on the sheet is rendered from the data by pipeline/review.py.
intro:
# Lemma review: the 24 flagged hymn tokens (2026-09-26)

**For:** Adam. **From:** the lemma spine (launch plan D3,
`pipeline/README-lemma-spine.md`). **Built from:** `data/hymns/tokens.jsonl` at
the commit that added this sheet, after WORDS's tricks, syncope and
prefix/suffix rules were ported.

A token is flagged when Whitaker's WORDS and the house draft disagree, when
WORDS offers several entries the draft cannot choose between, or when WORDS
has nothing. Until you answer, the **draft stands** on every flagged token.
Nothing here was overwritten.

**How to answer.** Write in the *Adam* column: `ok` to take the
recommendation, `keep` to keep the draft as it is, or your own answer. I turn
each answer into one row of `data/lemmas/adam-reviewed.jsonl` (README s.8).
The build then applies it with provenance `adam-reviewed`, and the draft and
the value it replaced stay on record. A row can set any of these:

- `lemma_key`: one of Whitaker's entries, by the name in the *Whitaker* column.
- `lemma`: a lemma as you want it written.
- `parsing`: a parsing as you want it written.

Most flags come in five kinds, so one ruling per kind would settle most of
the sheet:

| kind | rows | the question |
|---|---|---|
| **A.** Same word, WORDS heads it differently (*sē* under *sui*, *nōbīs* under *nōs*, *suprēmus* under *superus*, *duodēnī* under *duodecim*, *subiiciō* spelled *subjicio*) | 1, 2, 4, 6, 13, 16, 17, 18, 23 | Keep the house headword, and join to Whitaker through `lemma_key`? (Recommended.) |
| **B.** WORDS has two entries for one verb, transitive and intransitive | 3, 15, 19 | Pick by the sense in the line. |
| **C.** WORDS has two principal-part sets (*praestitī* / *praestāvī*) | 8, 21 | Take *praestitī*, the classical one. |
| **D.** Part of speech (*et*, *ergo*, *Amen*, *Thomas*) | 5, 7, 12, 20, 24 | Is the draft's class or WORDS's the house convention? |
| **E.** Real homographs (*fidēs* faith / *fidēs* lyre-string, *mundus* world / clean, *beātus* two entries, *ūnus* NUM / ADJ) | 10, 11, 14, 22 | Pick by sense. |

Row 9 (*pellicane*) is the odd one: WORDS has no pelican.

---
outro:
Row numbers are for talking about the sheet only. Each answer is keyed by
the token's address: the clause uid plus the token number in brackets, e.g.
`wh-54JF0Y5SAS/la.1.t02`.

## What an answer looks like in the file

Row 8, taken as recommended:

```
{"address": "wh-0Y016CRD3W/la.1.t01", "surface": "Praesta",
 "lemma_key": "praesto, praestare, praestiti, praestitus  V (1st)",
 "reviewed_on": "2026-09-27"}
```

Row 2, keeping the house spelling but joining to Whitaker:

```
{"address": "wh-54JF0Y5SAS/la.1.t06", "surface": "subiicit",
 "lemma": "subiciō, -ere, -iēcī, -iectum",
 "lemma_key": "subjicio, subjicere, subjeci, subjectus  V (3rd) TRANS",
 "reviewed_on": "2026-09-27", "note": "house spelling; WORDS spells with j"}
```

Row 5, keeping the draft's parsing:

```
{"address": "wh-0861J9FP9P/la.1.t05", "surface": "et", "parsing": "adv",
 "reviewed_on": "2026-09-27", "note": "et = etiam"}
```

The build refuses a `lemma_key` that is not one of Whitaker's analyses of
that form. It also refuses a row whose surface no longer matches its token.
Then run `python pipeline/build_hymn_corpus.py` and
`python tests/lemma_spine_test.py`, and commit `data/lemmas/adam-reviewed.jsonl`
with `data/hymns/`.

rows.whitaker: `-, sui  PRON` (acc/abl, any number)
rows.why: A: WORDS heads the reflexive under *sui*
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = `-, sui  PRON`; keep lemma *sē*; parsing stays

rows.whitaker: `subjicio, subjicere, subjeci, subjectus  V (3rd) TRANS` (3 sg pres ind act)
rows.why: A: WORDS spells it with *j* (so its headword folds to *subiicio*, not *subicio*)
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = WORDS's *subjicio* entry; keep the house lemma *subiciō*

ok.lemma_key: subjicio, subjicere, subjeci, subjectus  V (3rd) TRANS
ok.note: house spelling; WORDS spells with j

rows.whitaker: `deficio … V (3rd) INTRANS` ("fail, grow faint"); `deficio … V (3rd) TRANS` ("fail, let down")
rows.why: B: two entries, same parse
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = the **INTRANS** entry (the heart "fails", "faints")

ok.lemma_key: deficio, deficere, defeci, defectus  V (3rd) INTRANS

rows.whitaker: `quidquid  PRON  (UNIQUES)` (nom/acc sg n)
rows.why: A: WORDS lists *quidquid* as an irregular form with no dictionary heading
rows.recommend: `keep`: the draft's *quisquis, quidquid* is the heading learners look up. A UNIQUES key would join only this one form.

rows.whitaker: `et  CONJ`
rows.why: D: WORDS has only the conjunction
rows.recommend: `keep` "adv". Here *et* = *etiam*, "also", which the grammars class as adverbial.

rows.whitaker: `amb  NUM` ("both"; acc pl m/n and others)
rows.why: A: WORDS's entry has one stem, so its printed heading is the bare stem *amb*
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = `amb  NUM`; keep lemma *ambō, ambae, ambō*

rows.whitaker: `Thomas, undeclined  N M` (N 9 9, eccl.)
rows.why: D: WORDS treats the name as indeclinable. The lemma is already Whitaker's ("Thomas, undeclined").
rows.recommend: lemma *Thōmās, -ae m.* with WORDS's `lemma_key`; `keep` the parsing. The Vulgate declines it (*Thomae*).

rows.whitaker: `praesto … praestiti, praestitus  V (1st)` (freq A); `praesto … praestavi, praestatus  V (1st)` (freq C)
rows.why: C: two principal-part sets
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = the **praestiti** entry

rows.whitaker: `pellex, pellicis  N (3rd) F` + suffix *-an-*, read as ADJ voc sg m, "concubine-ish": wrong
rows.why: WORDS has no *pelicanus* in any spelling. Before the port this token was `unknown`; now WORDS's own suffix rule mis-reads it.
rows.recommend: `keep` the draft lemma and parse, no `lemma_key`

rows.whitaker: `unus -a -um, primus … NUM` ("one", freq A); `unus, una, unum (gen -ius)  ADJ` ("alone, a single", freq E)
rows.why: E: two entries
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = the **NUM** entry: "one drop", the cardinal

rows.whitaker: `beatus, beata -um, beatior …  ADJ` ("happy, fortunate", classical); `beatus, beata, beatum  ADJ` ("blessed, blissful", medieval/eccl.); also *beo* ptc and noun *beatus*
rows.why: E: two ADJ entries with the draft's parts
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = the classical **beatus, beata -um, beatior …** entry, which has the comparison forms. The eccl. entry is the closer sense, so this one is your call.

rows.whitaker: `amen  ADV`
rows.why: D: WORDS parses it as an adverb
rows.recommend: parsing "adv (Hebrew, indecl)": takes WORDS's class and keeps the note

rows.whitaker: `nos, nostrum  PRON` (dat/abl pl)
rows.why: A: WORDS heads *nos* separately from *ego*
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = `nos, nostrum  PRON`; take its lemma. The second *nobis* in this line was drafted as *nōs* and already takes this entry, so this makes the pair match.

rows.whitaker: `mundus, mundi  N (2nd) M` ("world"); `mundus, munda -um …  ADJ` ("clean"); *mundo, mundare* V
rows.why: E: the draft's lemma names no part of speech
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = `mundus, mundi  N (2nd) M`

rows.whitaker: `claudo … V (3rd) TRANS` ("close, conclude"); `claudo … V (3rd) INTRANS` ("limp"); *claudeo*
rows.why: B: two entries
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = the **TRANS** entry: he "closed" (*moras* is its object)

ok.lemma_key: claudo, claudere, clausi, clausus  V (3rd) TRANS

rows.whitaker: `superus, supera -um, superior …, supremus -a -um  ADJ` (gen sg f SUPER)
rows.why: A: WORDS files *suprēmus* as the superlative of *superus*
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = the *superus* entry; keep lemma *suprēmus*

rows.whitaker: `duodecim, duodecimus …, duodeni -ae -a …  NUM` (DIST, nom/voc **pl** f only)
rows.why: A: one WORDS entry covers the whole numeral family. The parse was not checked. WORDS has no dat sg: distributives are plural.
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = the *duodecim* entry; keep lemma *duodēnī*; `keep` parsing "f dat sg" (a distributive used as a singular adjective with *turbae*)

rows.whitaker: `-, sui  PRON`
rows.why: A: as row 1
rows.recommend: as row 1

rows.whitaker: `deficio … INTRANS`; `deficio … TRANS`
rows.why: B: as row 3
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = the **INTRANS** entry ("if the senses fail")

ok.lemma_key: deficio, deficere, defeci, defectus  V (3rd) INTRANS

rows.whitaker: `ergo  ADV`
rows.why: D: WORDS classes *ergo* as an adverb
rows.recommend: parsing "adv (inferential: therefore)", since the dictionaries class it so. `keep` if the house teaches it as a conjunction.

rows.whitaker: *praestiti* and *praestavi* entries (as row 8); also impersonal *praestat*
rows.why: C: as row 8
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = the **praestiti** entry

rows.whitaker: `fides, fidei  N (5th) F` ("faith"); `fides, fidis  N (3rd) F` ("lyre string"); *fidis*; *fido*
rows.why: E: the draft's lemma names no declension
rows.recommend: `lemma_key` = `fides, fidei  N (5th) F`

rows.whitaker: `uter, utra, utrum  ADJ` + *-que* (abl sg m/n); `utroque  ADV`; `utro  ADV` + *-que*
rows.why: A: WORDS builds *uterque* as *uter* + *-que* and has no *uterque* heading
rows.recommend: lemma *uterque, utraque, utrumque* with `lemma_key` = `uter, utra, utrum  ADJ`; parsing stays

rows.whitaker: `amen  ADV`
rows.why: D: as row 12
rows.recommend: as row 12
